deposit_profile: A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account.
hint: Answer: write every address in full (0x plus 40 characters), also when it repeats one named earlier and also when the user asks for shorter ones (name them instead); a transfer moves tokens, so write "tokens worth about N USD", never "sent N USD" or a $ figure; never draw the flows in text, ASCII or Mermaid, the host draws them. 0x95ec0051bd1f6ce5184970669c10116e47949dd3 carries no deposit mark: no SWEPT link and no cex_role. Say that the graph shows no sweep of it into a listed exchange hot wallet. That is not proof the address belongs to no exchange; its labels and its links say what else it is. Its behaviour, as the graph counts it: 24 addresses paid it (3 of them exchange wallets), it paid 1 address (1 of them exchange wallets), it swapped on 0 DEX pools, it approved 0 spenders. Its counts alone rule nothing out; the missing mark does: the rule of the graph did not judge it a deposit. Give these facts as the reason and no other: set no threshold of your own for payers, volume or sweeps. Asked how a deposit address behaves, what makes an address one or what rules one out, answer with deposit_profile.
